pick: Chip-verified physical outputs with on-chain redemption state
why_our_call: Plotters are rising (46 projects), post-mint params are new (2025), and physical redemption went quiet after Feb 2024: the link between token and object is the weakest point.
cheap_test_srb: Chip 10 pen plots with NTAG424 tags; write a testnet post-mint flag 'physical: issued / chip UID'; the live view shows 'plotted'. [SRB]
our_data: Plotter 46 rising; physical redemption 6, none after 2024; PMP 3 (2025)

why_our_call: 191 projects already read the clock and the share is rising, so a large catalogue fits a low-power frame; e-ink has no artist-native edition yet.
cheap_test_srb: Waveshare 7.3-inch colour e-ink + ESP32 (≈$100 [estimate]) running a p5 sketch that renders hourly; show it at an Art Blocks event. [SRB]

why_our_call: LIFT (ROM in token, 2025) and mio (2026, off Art Blocks) show live momentum around this exact studio; the risk is that each build is bespoke.
cheap_test_srb: Flash LIFT-style ROMs onto 10 reproduction GBA carts, or an ESP32 + small OLED kit, as a redemption for one Factory project. [SRB]
our_data: ROM in token 1 (2025); custom hardware 0 on-chain

pick: Risograph and darkroom editions as the affordable physical tier
why_our_call: Prints and screen prints are fading on Art Blocks while risograph has 2 guessed projects: the cheapest unique-per-sheet format is nearly empty.
cheap_test_srb: 50-sheet riso run of 50 different outputs from one project; measure cost per sheet and collector uptake. [SRB]

why_our_call: Unused on Art Blocks, but webcam/mic input faded after 2024, so permission-gated inputs have a poor track record; a separate sensor box sidesteps that.
cheap_test_srb: $20–40 PM2.5/CO₂ sensor [estimate] on an ESP32 feeding a WebSocket into an existing p5 token. [SRB]

why_our_call: Nothing token-linked found; 7 tokens already act as fabrication files, so the export side is solved.
cheap_test_srb: Send 3 STL exports from an .obj-capable token to a ceramic-printing studio; compare cost and failure rate. [SRB]

why_our_call: Totem shows heartbeat data works; capture-once avoids long-term health data.
cheap_test_srb: Web mint page that reads heart rate from the phone camera (finger on lens) and seeds parameters; pilot at a live event. [SRB]

pick: Spatial / WebXR wrappers for three.js tokens
why_our_call: 84 three.js projects (flat) could gain XR, but A-Frame has had no AB use since 2021: demand is unproven.
cheap_test_srb: Generic WebXR viewer loading any Art Blocks three.js token in a Quest or Vision Pro browser; check 5 projects render. [SRB]

why_our_call: INK is the only example; fun, but hard to make deterministic.
cheap_test_srb: A perfumer maps 3 parameters to accords; 6 samples; blind-match test with collectors. [SRB]

pick: Robot-arm live performance as a minting event
why_our_call: Proven in art, absent on Art Blocks, and the most expensive test here.
cheap_test_srb: Hobby arm (≈$300–2,000 [estimate]) or a university lab draws the token's SVG live; record the stream hash on-chain. [SRB]

pick: Tokens as agents: a generative piece that is also an agent with its own wallet
srb_confidence: not an SRB pick (Shawn's idea, unranked)
why_our_call: No Art Blocks use found. 721T (on ERC-8048) gives a token agent context and endpoints, ERC-6551 gives it a wallet, and Loopers (2026-09-18) shows the stack in use outside art. Unproven demand, so we keep it out of the ranking.
cheap_test_srb: Our test, not SRB's: on a testnet, give one generative token a 721T context key and web endpoint, plus an ERC-6551 account; check that a collector can find it and that it can hold one other token.
